transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I'm here because... what really scared me enough to make an appointment is that I’ve started having these thoughts lately. Just thinking things like, it would be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. 

I want to be clear that I don’t have any actual plan to harm myself or anything like that. But just having that thought cross my mind at all... it was enough to make me realize I needed to come in and talk to someone.
When did you first start noticing these thoughts about not waking up? Was this something that came on suddenly over days or weeks, or has this been building up over a longer period of time?
It's been building up for a while now. I'd say this has been going on for about eight months. It really started around the time my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly.
Over these past eight months, how would you describe your overall mood most days? Are you feeling persistently sad or down, or is it more that you're feeling anxious and worried?

I would say it is more of a persistent sadness, rather than anxiety. Most days, I feel as if a... well, a gray film has settled over everything. Even when I’m just doing simple things, like making a cup of tea or looking out at my garden, there’s this quiet heaviness in me. It is just always there, and I can’t quite reason my way out of it.
Before these eight months, have you ever experienced a period like this before—where you felt persistently sad and down for weeks or months at a time?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've had normal ups and downs throughout my life, of course, but nothing like this. I've never felt this kind of constant sadness before these last eight months.

Just to make sure I have this right: other than this 8-month period you're describing now, have you ever had a time in your life—even if it was shorter—where you felt depressed or down for at least two weeks in a row?
No, I really haven't. Like I said, it's just been these past eight months. Before that, I never had a time where I felt down like this for two weeks straight. This is... this is all new for me.

During these past 8 months or even before, have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your thoughts were racing—even if it only lasted a few days?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've always been a fairly steady person, so I've never felt unusually energetic or had racing thoughts. And I've always needed my regular amount of sleep. So, no, nothing like that at all.
Besides the persistent sadness you've described, over these past 8 months have you noticed changes in your appetite or weight?
No, my appetite has been about the same. I haven't noticed any weight loss or gain, either. I'm still eating my regular meals, so nothing has really changed in that area.
Over these past 8 months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep? For example, are you sleeping more than usual, or are you having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Well, yes, my sleep has definitely changed. I just... I don't sleep well at all anymore. Getting to sleep is uneven, I guess you could say. And then I almost always wake up around three or four in the morning. I just lie there, and my mind starts going over all these things... like phone calls I need to make, or forms I have to fill out, or I just worry about whether I handled something correctly the day before. Because of all that, by the time morning comes, I just feel like I've hardly rested at all.

Over these past 8 months, have you noticed that things you normally enjoyed doing—hobbies, spending time with friends or family, activities you found fun—have stopped bringing you pleasure or interest?

Yes, I have noticed that. I've always enjoyed painting—watercolors, mostly. Lately, I'll still set out all my supplies sometimes, but then I just sit there staring at the blank paper. I usually end up putting it all away without doing anything because... well, the pleasure I used to feel in the colors and the light, it just doesn't seem to arrive anymore. So, yes, the interest just isn't there like it used to be.
Over these past 8 months, have you found it harder to concentrate or make decisions than you normally do?

No, I haven't really noticed any trouble with that. I can still sit down and read a book or follow along with the news without losing my place. And making decisions... no, that hasn't been an issue either. I think my focus is about the same as it always has been.
During these past 8 months, have you found yourself feeling guilty about things, or feeling like you're worthless or a burden to others?

Yes, I have been dealing with a fair amount of guilt. It's mostly regarding my brother. I just keep going back over his decline in my head, and... well, I keep telling myself that if I had been a better sister, or just more attentive to him, I would have noticed what was happening sooner. I feel like I might have been able to prevent some of it.

When you think about the guilt you're feeling regarding your brother, is that the main area where you're blaming yourself, or do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself in other areas of your life as well?

No, it's really just about my brother. I don't feel worthless in general or anything like that. It's just... I keep going back over his decline, you know? I just keep telling myself that if I had been a better sister, or if I had just been more attentive, I would have noticed what was happening sooner. I just feel like I could have prevented some of this if I had paid better attention. But outside of that, no, I don't really feel guilty about other things.

You mentioned that your brother's health and behavior changed around the time your sadness began. Looking back over these 8 months, would you say your sadness has been directly connected to thinking about your brother and what happened to him, or does the sadness feel like it's there regardless of whether you're thinking about him or not?

Well, it's... it's there regardless, really. I mean, yes, I think about him a lot, but the sadness doesn't just go away when I'm not. Most days, I just feel like this... this gray film has settled over everything. Even when I'm doing something simple, like making a cup of tea or just looking out at my garden, there's just this quiet heaviness inside me. It's just there, and I can't quite reason my way out of it, no matter what I'm thinking about.
